shorts.title: What you will learn: Dynamic arrays
shorts.hook: The user decides the size, and the array fits.
shorts.script: The user decides the size, and the array fits. Today the user chooses the size. A plain array cannot do this, but an array on the heap can. A plain array needs a size that the compiler knows. An array on the heap can use a size that you read at run time. Use new with the size in square brackets. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: Dynamic arrays.

shorts.title: Dynamic arrays in one minute
shorts.hook: A plain array needs a size that the compiler knows.
shorts.script: A plain array needs a size that the compiler knows. An array on the heap can use a size that you read at run time. Use new with the size in square brackets. You must free it with delete square brackets. You must also remember its size yourself. This is why most programmers prefer a vector. Think of a tailor. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Dynamic arrays in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.hook: A vector with n items does the same job.
shorts.script: A vector with n items does the same job. We fill it in the same way. A range-based for works too. There is no new and no delete. The vector frees its own memory. It also knows its size. Type four and press Enter. The program prints one, four, nine and sixteen. New with a size makes an array of any size at run time. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: Delete on a pointer to a local
shorts.hook: Can you spot the bug in dynamic arrays?
shorts.script: Can you spot the bug in dynamic arrays? Bug of the Day. We call delete on n, which is a plain int. The compiler says the type int was given to delete, but a pointer is expected. Delete must get the pointer that new returned. Here that is a, and it needs square brackets. Delete needs a pointer. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: Delete on a pointer to a local.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: Can you average of n numbers in dynamic arrays?
shorts.script: Can you average of n numbers in dynamic arrays? A tailor and a programmer have one thing in common. They both measure twice and cut once. Ask for n. Make a vector of n numbers, read them, and print their average. Write your answer in the comments. New with a size makes an array of any size at run time. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Pun and challenge.
